newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Oct durables suggest manufacturing healthy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Oct durables suggest manufacturing healthy.

text.p: A stronger than expected durable goods report for October suggests that manufacturing activity remains healthy, economists said on Wednesday.

The Commerce Department reported that new orders for durable goods rose 0.1 percent in October, well above the 2.0 percent decline analysts had forecast. That follows a 4.6 percent jump in September, revised from a 4.9 percent gain.
"It's a good, healthy report for the real side of the economy," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.

Economists said they were mildly surprised that transportation orders fell only 7.9 percent last month, after a 19.0 percent rise in September. Aircraft orders were expected to fall off more, and the Canadian Auto Workers strike was seen having a deeper impact.
"It is difficult to estimate the extent transportation affects the overall index," said Chris Iggo, chief economist at BZW Securities Inc.
Durable goods ex-transportation rose 2.9 percent in October. "There's nothing (in the report) that suggests any further problems for industry," Iggo said.
The October durable goods rise, while small, was the third in four months, a rare feat, given the volatile nature of the series, where large month-to-month swings are common.

Economists noted that the October orders increase was concentrated in motors, transformers and electrical equipment. Electronic/electrical equipment orders were up 17.3 percent in October, the highest gain on record.
Meanwhile, non-defense capital goods orders excluding aircraft rose 1.6 percent in October, after a 2.2 percent increase in September.
"These are strong gains," Liro said. "There are no givebacks in the corporate investment program."
Liro added that he wouldn't be surprised if goods orders show another rise in November.

"The economy is in good shape in the fourth quarter," said John Ryding, senior economist at Bear Stearns & Co. "We had a buildup in inventories in the fourth quarter, but order growth is robust in the fourth quarter. And, the order component of the Chicago purchasers report improved further in November. Things are just hunky dory as far as the manufacturing outlook goes."
